result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS (result.status PASS: no applicable invariant fails). Scope test: IN SCOPE by the tenant-data clause. The diff changes the value written by the autosave write path to session_answer, a tenant-scoped entity, reached through the existing PUT /exam-sessions/:id/answers/:question_id route. No route, migration, secret, response shape or lookup-by-ID handler is changed. APPLIES: INV-1 (PASS), INV-4 (PASS), INV-7 (PASS), INV-8 (PASS). NOT-APPLICABLE: INV-2, INV-3, INV-5, INV-6, INV-9, INV-10. Points (a)-(f) hold as stated for the per-value upper bound. The findings are: the bound is per question, so the sum across questions is not bounded by the span (F1); a comment overstates monotonicity for over-large legacy rows (F2); the over-large test asserts <= 30 rather than the exact bound (F3); plus INFO-level notes. None is an invariant violation. Read-only: no mix or BEAM was run; file reads, git and grep only. The lint of this handoff was not run (no mix); the file was checked by a JSON parse only.

evidence.a_client_cannot_move_bound: PASS. The router schema (lib/letflow/modules/exam/router.ex:407-411) accepts only selected_option_ids, time_spent_seconds and text_answer; answer_attrs (router.ex:420-425) carries only those keys. autosave_answer (session.ex:510-519) reads only question_id, selected_option_ids, time_spent_seconds and Map.get of text_answer; no client started_at is read. started_at is the server row's value: session.ex:538 parse_dt!(fv(session, 'started_at')), where session comes from fetch_session (session.ex:523, 923-928, Latest.get by session_id under prefix). started_at is written only at create, from iso8601(utc_now()) (session.ex:750). The bound is session.ex:1097-1100: elapsed = max(DateTime.diff(now, started_at, :second), 0); min(max(stored, received), elapsed). The value is never above elapsed. Non-integer and negative input is rejected before the bound by check_non_negative (session.ex:522, 915-921: is_integer and >= 0, else :answer_shape_invalid). Residual dependency on the session row's integrity is recorded as F7.
evidence.b_clamp_vs_span: PASS for the per-value bound. Each written value satisfies stored <= elapsed at its own compute time (session.ex:1099). Elapsed is non-decreasing, so a stored value never exceeds the session's wall-clock span at any later time. The aggregate across questions is NOT bounded by the span, because the bound applies per row (F1). Rows written before this change had no bound and can exceed elapsed; the next save lowers them (F2).

All three writes carry prefix (session.ex:1049-1053, 1069, 1082). The diff adds no tenant_id attribute and no migration. issues.description: lib/letflow/modules/exam/session.ex:1097-1100 (bounded_time_spent) and the comment at 1091-1096: the bound applies per stored value, not per session. Each answered question can carry up to elapsed seconds, so the sum across k questions can reach k times the session's wall-clock span. The comment's claim that the value cannot exceed the time the session has existed is true per question only. No reader in lib/ sums the field and no scoring or anti-cheat reader exists (check e), so the impact is limited to the integrity of a reporting field. Not an invariant violation. Fix direction: if the value is ever summed, shown as a total or used as a timing signal, bound the cross-question sum (for example, cap each save at elapsed minus the other questions' stored totals), or record the per-question semantics in the exam design doc.

lib/letflow/modules/exam/session.ex:1093-1094 says the stored value never decreases (max with what is stored). In the code the min is applied after the max (session.ex:1099), so a stored value above elapsed is lowered on the next save. This can occur only for rows written before this change, which had no bound: the pre-change upsert stored any non-negative integer (session.ex:522 and 915-921). The direction of the change is correct, but the comment is inaccurate for that case. The added tests (test/letflow/modules/exam/session_test.exs:1590-1600) do not cover a legacy over-large row. Fix direction: correct the comment; optionally add a test that seeds an over-large row and checks the next save lowers it to elapsed.

test/letflow/modules/exam/session_test.exs:1607-1608: the over-large test asserts stored < 999_999 and stored <= 30. A bound that is off by up to 30 seconds, for example elapsed + 30, would pass. The assertion does not pin the bound the test is named for. Fix direction: assert equality with the elapsed seconds at save time, computed from the session's started_at read back from the row, or assert stored <= DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), started_at, :second).

test/letflow/modules/exam/session_test.exs:954 (Process.sleep(11_000)) and :1593 (Process.sleep(2_100)): wall-clock waits add about 13 seconds to the suite. The 11-second wait is a precondition so that the existing exact assertion (== 10, line 998) still holds under the bound. The expected value is unchanged, so this is not a weakening of that test. A clock seam would avoid the wait.

lib/letflow/modules/exam/session.ex:1049-1070: the upsert is read-then-write. Two concurrent autosaves on the same question can interleave so that the lower value wins, which defeats the max within that race. The upper bound still holds, because every written value is computed from its own now and started_at. The pattern is pre-existing and not introduced by this diff.
issues.owner: ELIXIR-DEV, only if the monotonic claim is ever made a hard guarantee

issues.description: web/src/modules/exam/ExamSessionPage.tsx:204 and :216: the optimistic state stores the value that was sent, not the value the server stored after clamping. The next save sends the base plus measured time again and the server clamps again. The server stays authoritative; the UI can show a larger value than is stored until reload.

Pre-existing, not in this diff: the started_at bound depends on no candidate-reachable path writing the session record. CANDIDATE holds exactly six exam permissions (lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex:150-159; core_role_allows?(:CANDIDATE, _) is false at line 1479), none of them :EntitiesRecordsWrite, which gates PUT /entities/records/:entity_type/:record_id (lib/letflow/routers/entities.ex:297-298). This review did not enumerate every other role's grant. A future grant of :EntitiesRecordsWrite to a role a candidate can hold would let the candidate move started_at and defeat the bound. Re-check on any role-matrix change.
